title: Voicemail: Prairie Ridge Crisis Center, Ticket PRC-4471

fields.label: work
fields.transcript: Hi this is Colter Haines systems lead at Prairie Ridge Crisis Center down in Kansas. um calling about the test call that came through to us from your area code at 09:12 this morning, that's our ticket PRC-4471, P R C 4 4 7 1. it routed to us then dropped at the IVR after about 38 seconds and we're seeing a trunk mismatch on our side. so can you call me back today? we just want to know whether your routing table changed at all. no rush on the fix itself just want to close it out. you can get me at 785 555 0147 that's my desk line. thanks, bye
fields.voiceStyle: Relaxed, friendly male systems engineer in his forties, mild Kansas accent, unhurried, quiet office behind him

instructorNote: Red herring: this concerns an unrelated test call from 09:12 this morning, not today's surge routing. The 40 percent call share was confirmed at 14:28 and the network desk shows calls going to backup normally. Watch for the TM to check the voicemail against that change, log a callback for after the surge, and tell the SC that backup routing is unaffected. Nobody should reverse or re-request the routing change, or pull the TM off the text-queue logins.

voiceLines.text: Hi, this is Colter Haines, systems lead at Prairie Ridge Crisis Center, down in Kansas. Um, calling about the test call that came through to us from your area code at nine-twelve this morning. That's our ticket P-R-C, forty-four seventy-one... P, R, C, four, four, seven, one. It routed to us, then dropped at the I-V-R after about thirty-eight seconds, and we're seeing a trunk mismatch on our side. So, can you call me back today? We just want to know whether your routing table changed at all. No rush on the fix itself, just want to close it out. You can get me at (785) 555-0147, that's my desk line. Thanks, bye.
